q: An accounts clerk has to book ordinary working expenses of a commercial line for the month. Under which Major Head will the expenditure be classified?
e: Major Head 3002 covers revenue expenditure (working expenses) of commercial lines; 1002 is earnings and 5002 is capital outlay.

q: While compiling a minor head, the clerk finds revenue credits of Rs 12,450 to be adjusted. There is no separate receipt head inside the expense classification for this. The credits should be shown:

options.A: Under PU 27 as a plus figure
options.B: Under PU 98 as a minus figure
options.C: Under a new PU created by the zonal railway

e: Revenue credits are booked under PU 98 and shown as minus figures within the expense classification.

q: For compiling the Stores Budget, the GM-approved figures for cost of materials from stock have to be sent to the Stores branch. Under which Primary Unit are the stores-budget figures communicated?
e: Stores-budget figures are communicated under PU 27, which covers cost of materials from stock.

q: A zonal railway proposes to create a new Primary Unit locally to capture a new type of expense, without any central prescription. This proposal is:

options.B: Permissible, as PUs are zonal subjects
options.D: Not permissible, as the PU list is centrally prescribed and uniform for all zonal railways

e: Classification is prescribed in Finance Code Vol-II; the PU list is uniform and a zonal railway cannot create new PUs.

q: Government contribution for UPS subscribers working on a strategic line has to be booked under the heads opened by ACS No. 13. The correct home for the booking is:

options.A: Major Head 3003, Sub-Major Head 11, Abstract O
options.D: Major Head 3002, Sub-Major Head 11, Abstract O

e: ACS No. 13 opened UPS Government-contribution heads under both 3002 and 3003 at Sub-Major Head 11, Abstract O; a strategic line falls under 3003.

q:
Consider the following statements about Major Head 3002:
1. Its Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12 correspond to Abstracts A to M.
2. The letter I is skipped in the abstract series.
3. There are thirteen abstracts for twelve Sub-Major Heads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Twelve Sub-Major Heads map to twelve abstracts A to M with I skipped, so there are twelve, not thirteen, abstracts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Credits under PU 98 are shown as minus figures.
2. Stores-budget figures are communicated under PU 27.
3. PU 27 covers cost of materials by direct purchase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: PU 98 carries credits as minus figures and PU 27 is the stores-budget / materials-from-stock unit; direct purchase is PU 28.

q:
Consider the following statements about prescription of classification:
1. Classification is centrally prescribed in Finance Code Vol-II.
2. The list of Primary Units is uniform for all zonal railways.
3. A zonal railway can create new Primary Units for local needs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: The classification and PU list are centrally prescribed and uniform; zonal creation of PUs is not permitted.

q:
Consider the following statements about the UPS heads opened by ACS No. 13:
1. They cover Government contribution of UPS subscribers.
2. They were opened under Major Heads 3002 and 3003.
3. They were opened under Sub-Major Head 12, Abstract M.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: ACS No. 13 opened the UPS Government-contribution heads under 3002 and 3003 at Sub-Major Head 11, Abstract O, not SMH 12.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriation to the Pension Fund is charged under Sub-Major Head 12, Abstract M.
2. Pension actually paid is booked under Sub-Major Head 11, Abstract L.
3. Both appropriation and payment are booked under the same Sub-Major Head.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Appropriation and payment are deliberately split: appropriation in SMH 12 / Abstract M, payment in SMH 11 / Abstract L.

q:
Consider the following statements about Major Heads:
1. Major Head 1002 covers earnings of commercial lines.
2. Major Head 1003 covers earnings of strategic lines.
3. Major Head 5002 covers capital outlay of commercial lines.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: All three mappings are correct in the master table of Major Heads.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Major Head 3001 has no Sub-Major Heads and divides straight into Minor Heads.
2. Surveys for a new line are charged under Major Head 3001, Minor Head 005.
3. Major Head 3001 covers working expenses of commercial lines.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: 3001 is the odd one out with no Sub-Major Heads; working expenses of commercial lines belong to 3002, not 3001.

q:
Consider the following statements about earnings abstracts:
1. Abstract X covers coaching earnings, including luggage and parcels.
2. Abstract Y covers goods earnings.
3. Abstract Z covers sundry other earnings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: X is coaching (luggage X-300, parcels X-400), Y is goods, and Z is sundry other earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements about works classification:
1. Under Major Heads 5002 and 5003, Plan Heads function as Minor Heads.
2. In the codified capital classification, the first two digits denote the source of finance.
3. In the codified capital classification, the last two digits denote the Primary Unit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: All three describe the allocation code: Plan Head as Minor Head, source first, PU last.

q: Which letter is skipped in the Abstracts A to M corresponding to Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12 of Major Head 3002?
e: The letter I is skipped, giving twelve abstracts A to M for twelve Sub-Major Heads.

q: The detailed classification of Major Heads, Sub-Major Heads and Primary Units for Indian Railways is prescribed in which publication?
e: The lists are prescribed in the Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume II.

q: Appropriations to funds created out of railway surplus are budgeted under which Major Head?
e: Major Head 3006 covers funds created out of surplus / appropriations to funds from railway surplus.

q: Which of the following statements about Abstracts K, L and M is NOT correct?

options.A: Abstract K covers Miscellaneous Working Expenses
options.B: Abstract K covers General Management expenditure
options.C: Abstract L covers Provident Fund, Pension and Other Retirement Benefits actually paid
options.D: Abstract M covers Appropriations to Funds

e: Abstract K does not cover General Management expenditure; that is a stated bank trap.

q: Which of the following statements about the UPS heads under ACS No. 13 is NOT correct?

options.A: They were opened vide RBA No. 09/2025
options.B: They relate to Government contribution of UPS subscribers
options.C: They were opened only under Major Head 5002
options.D: They sit under Sub-Major Head 11, Abstract O

e: The heads were opened under Major Heads 3002 and 3003, not only under 5002.

q:
Assertion (A): There are twelve abstracts for the twelve Sub-Major Heads of Major Head 3002, although the series runs from A to M.
Reason (R): The letter I is skipped in the abstract series.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Skipping I is exactly why A to M yields twelve abstracts, matching SMH 01-12.

q:
Assertion (A): Revenue credits are shown as minus figures in the expense compilation.
Reason (R): Credits under PU 98 are booked within the expense classification instead of under a separate receipt head.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: PU 98 is the mechanism that produces the minus-figure presentation stated in A.

q:
Assertion (A): A zonal railway may create a new Primary Unit when a new object of expenditure arises.
Reason (R): The list of Primary Units is uniform for all zonal railways and is centrally prescribed.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is false; R is true and in fact bars the local creation asserted in A.

q:
Assertion (A): UPS Government-contribution heads exist under both commercial-lines and strategic-lines revenue heads.
Reason (R): ACS No. 13 opened the heads under Major Heads 3002 and 3003 at Sub-Major Head 11, Abstract O.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: 3002 is commercial and 3003 is strategic, so R directly establishes A.

q:
Match the Abstract with its subject:
I. A  II. B  III. H  IV. J
a. Repairs and Maintenance - Permanent Way and Works
b. Staff Welfare and Amenities
c. General Superintendence and Services
d. Operating Expenses - Fuel
e: A is General Superintendence, B is P. Way and Works, H is Fuel, and J is Staff Welfare.

q:
Match the Abstract with its subject:
I. C  II. D  III. E  IV. F
a. Operating Expenses - Rolling Stock and Equipment
b. Repairs and Maintenance - Motive Power
c. Repairs and Maintenance - Carriages and Wagons
d. Repairs and Maintenance - Plant and Equipment
e: C is Motive Power, D is Carriages and Wagons, E is Plant and Equipment, and F is Rolling Stock and Equipment.

q:
Match the Abstract with its subject:
I. G  II. K  III. L  IV. M
a. Appropriations to Funds
b. Operating Expenses - Traffic
c. Provident Fund, Pension and Other Retirement Benefits actually paid
d. Miscellaneous Working Expenses
e: G is Traffic, K is Miscellaneous Working Expenses, L is pensionary charges paid, and M is Appropriations to Funds.

q:
Match the Major Head with what it covers:
I. 1002  II. 1003  III. 3002  IV. 3003
a. Revenue expenditure - strategic lines
b. Earnings of commercial lines
c. Revenue expenditure - commercial lines
d. Earnings of strategic lines
e: 1002 and 1003 are earnings of commercial and strategic lines; 3002 and 3003 are their revenue-expenditure counterparts.

q:
Match the Major Head with what it covers:
I. 3001  II. 3006  III. 5002  IV. 5003
a. Capital outlay - strategic lines
b. Policy Formulation, Direction, Research and Other Miscellaneous Organisations
c. Capital outlay - commercial lines
d. Funds created out of surplus
e: 3001 is policy and miscellaneous organisations, 3006 is surplus funds, and 5002/5003 are capital outlay for commercial/strategic lines.

q:
Match the Plan Head with the class of work:
I. 1100  II. 1500  III. 1600  IV. 3100
a. Track Renewals
b. New Lines
c. Doubling
d. Traffic Facilities
e: 1100 is New Lines, 1500 is Doubling, 1600 is Traffic Facilities, and 3100 is Track Renewals.

q:
Match the source-of-finance code with the source:
I. 20  II. 21  III. 25  IV. 26
a. Railway Safety Fund (RSF)
b. Capital (budgetary support)
c. Depreciation Reserve Fund (DRF)
d. Capital Fund
e: Code 20 is Capital, 21 is DRF, 25 is Capital Fund, and 26 is RSF.

q:
Match the source-of-finance code with the source:
I. 27  II. 29  III. 83  IV. 84
a. EBR-IRFC
b. Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF)
c. EBR-IF (institutional finance)
d. Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK)
e: Code 27 is SRSF, 29 is RRSK, 83 is EBR-IF, and 84 is EBR-IRFC.

q:
Match the revenue Primary Unit with the object (do not use the staff-pay units in dispute):
I. PU 01  II. PU 04  III. PU 16  IV. PU 27
a. Travelling Expenses
b. Salaries and Wages
c. Cost of materials from stock
d. House Rent Allowance
e: PU 01 is Salaries and Wages, PU 04 is HRA, PU 16 is Travelling Expenses, and PU 27 is materials from stock.

q:
Match the revenue Primary Unit with the object:
I. PU 28  II. PU 32  III. PU 50  IV. PU 51
a. Computer consumables, rental of computers and AMC - recurring
b. Cost of materials - direct purchase
c. Computer hardware, system and software - one-time
d. Contractual payments
e: PU 28 is direct purchase, PU 32 is contractual payments, PU 50 is one-time IT, and PU 51 is recurring IT.

q:
Match the works Primary Unit with the object:
I. PU 04  II. PU 05  III. PU 06  IV. PU 07
a. Stores supplied from stock
b. Credits for released materials
c. Direct supply of material
d. Freight on stores
e: In the works list, PU 04 is direct supply, PU 05 is stores from stock, PU 06 is freight on stores, and PU 07 is credits for released materials.

q:
Match the item with its correct classification home:
I. UPS Government contribution - commercial lines  II. UPS Government contribution - strategic lines  III. UPS Sub-Major Head  IV. UPS Abstract
a. Abstract O
b. Major Head 3003
c. Sub-Major Head 11
d. Major Head 3002
e: ACS No. 13 places UPS Government contribution under 3002 for commercial lines and 3003 for strategic lines, at SMH 11, Abstract O.
